results.content: With three months to go until the U.S. midterm elections in November, voters increasingly seem to prefer Democrats over the Republican Party that has had control of Congress for the last two years. Results of a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday showed that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate at present, compared to 37% for a Republican. The same survey also found that, for the first time in nearly a decade of its polling series, voters perceive the Democratic Party as having a better plan for the economy than the Republican Party. Registered voters are more likely to say they'll vote for Democrats than Republicans in this fall's congressional elections by a margin of 4 percentage points, according to the latest Economist / YouGov Poll. That's in line with the consistent single-digit leads for Democrats — usually low single digits — that Economist / YouGov surveys have found among registered voters over the past year.
